existing_kb_matches.label: def:degenerate_whittaker_setup
existing_kb_matches.statement: Given a nilpotent orbit O in g and f in O, choose a one-parameter subgroup phi: F^* -> G satisfying phi(s).f = s^-2 f for all s in F^*. Define U, respectively U', as the unipotent subgroup whose Lie algebra consists of those X such that lim_{s->0} phi(s).X = 0, respectively lim_{s->0} phi(s)s^-1.X = 0. Define U'' as the subgroup of U generated by U' and the stabilizer of f in U. The function gamma |-> psi(tr(f log gamma)) is a character of U'', denoted theta_f.

existing_kb_matches.label: def:degenerate_whittaker_forms
existing_kb_matches.statement: For a smooth representation (pi,W) and degenerate Whittaker setup (f,phi), W is said to admit a degenerate Whittaker model relative to (f,phi) if W_{U'',theta_f} is nonzero. The space W_{f,phi} of degenerate Whittaker forms on W relative to (f,phi) is defined by W_{U'',theta_f} when U = U'', and, when U != U'', by a Hom-space from the irreducible representation of the Heisenberg quotient U/(U'' intersection ker theta_f) with central character theta_f into W_{U'',theta_f}.

existing_kb_matches.label: def:whittaker_orbit_sets
existing_kb_matches.statement: Order nilpotent orbits by closure: O < O' means O is contained in the usual-topology closure of O'. For a representation pi with local character coefficients c_O, the paper introduces one set of nilpotent orbits O with c_O != 0 and a second set of nilpotent orbits containing an element f for which there exists a one-parameter subgroup phi satisfying phi(s).f = s^-2 f and W_{f,phi} != 0.

existing_kb_matches.label: ext:harish_chandra_local_character_expansion
existing_kb_matches.statement: For a smooth irreducible representation (pi,W) of G, there is a neighborhood of 1 in G identified by logarithm with a neighborhood of 0 in g on which the distribution character of pi has an expansion as a sum over nilpotent orbits O in g: tr pi = sum_O c_O times the Fourier transform of a suitably normalized invariant measure on O, with Fourier transform taken relative to psi composed with tr.

existing_kb_matches.label: ext:rodier_whittaker_model_criterion
existing_kb_matches.statement: Assume G is split. Let N be a maximal unipotent subgroup of G, T a torus normalizing N, and theta a nondegenerate character of N, meaning its stabilizer in T is the center of G. For the nilpotent orbit O containing the element f associated to theta by the source's pairing formula, a smooth irreducible representation (pi,W) admits a Whittaker model relative to theta if and only if c_O != 0. The source also reformulates this as existence of a maximal nilpotent orbit with nonzero coefficient.

existing_kb_matches.label: ext:moeglin_waldspurger_main_theorem
existing_kb_matches.statement: The main result of Chapter I says that the maximal elements of the nilpotent-orbit set defined by c_O != 0 coincide with the maximal elements of the nilpotent-orbit set defined by existence of nonzero W_{f,phi}. If O is a maximal element of either set, then c_O = dim W_{f,phi}, where f lies in O and phi is any one-parameter subgroup satisfying phi(s).f = s^-2 f.
